title: Availability Prioritizer and Deferred Credit Reconciler
author: Lina Kaur
release_notes: Adds an availability prioritizer that biases reservations toward low-risk tenants during constrained windows; introduces deferred credit reconciler to smooth reservation accounting; telemetry and alerts for headroom starvation. No API breakages.
commits_summary: 4 commits: 1) initial availability prioritizer prototype and interface; 2) deferred credit reconciler and reconciliation loop with dual-window accounting; 3) add telemetry counters, histograms and alerting rules; 4) tests and docs; commit messages: 'implement availability prioritizer core loop', 'deferred credit reconciler + safety probation', 'telemetry + alerts for headroom starvation', 'unit+integration tests and docs'.
description: Context: Several customers reported transient tail failures during cluster pressure where fair reservation allocation led to availability regressions for low-error tenants. Motivation: Reduce noisy preemption and avoid oscillation by preferring low-risk reservations while retaining fair long-term allocation. Solution summary: Introduce an Availability Prioritizer that computes a short-horizon score per-tenant based on recent error rates, criticality tag, and recent scale events; integrate a Deferred Credit Reconciler that delays hard reclamation of fractional reservation credits into a 'probation' window to smooth autoscaler reactions; expose telemetry and alerts to observe priority skew and reconciler lag. Key behaviors: - Short-horizon prioritization biases new reservations for low-risk tenants during constrained headroom windows. - Deferred credits accumulate in a pending ledger and are applied gradually using an exponentially-weighted decay to avoid sudden drops in available capacity. - Tenants on probation are given a temporary soft-decline path rather than immediate eviction; a time-based backoff reduces churn. - New config flags: autoscaler.priority_window_ms, reconciler.defer_window_seconds, reconciler.apply_rate, availability.probation_timeout. Implementation notes: Changes live primarily in pkg/autoscaler and pkg/alloc with a light control-plane hook in cmd/agent/config.yaml. priority_dispatcher.go implements scoring and admission, credit_reconciler.go runs reconciliation loop with concurrency-safe ledger, safety_net.go contains probation transitions. A small protobuf bump added a reservation field (pkg/api/v1/reservation.proto) guarded by a migration script. Tests and harness: Added integration/tenant_simulation_test.go to validate steady-state fairness under burst scenarios; unit tests for scoring and reconciler invariants. CI: Pipeline initially showed a flaky e2e due to timing in the simulation harness; adjusted test timeouts and reran — all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, e2e). Review summary: Marcos requested stronger invariants for ledger concurrency and an explicit metrics label for probation transitions; Ariel asked for clearer config docs and a safe default for deferred window; Devon suggested fallback to existing allocation if reconciler lag exceeds threshold. Author responses: Implemented a compare-and-swap ledger loop, added metric label 'probation_reason', documented defaults and added reconciler_lag_threshold config and safety fallback to admission flow. Operational considerations: Default flags are conservative; the pilot rollout should enable the feature for a small customer cohort under a feature gate. Telemetry: New metrics include autoscaler.availability_prioritizer.score (histogram), autoscaler.reconciler.pending_credits (gauge), autoscaler.reconciler.apply_rate (counter), autoscaler.probation.transitions (counter with label). Added alert autoscaler/HeadroomStarvation if reconciler_pending_credits > 0.5*cluster_capacity for >5m. Rollout plan: 1) Canary on Dedicated clusters with 2 tenants for 48h, 2) Expand to 20% of clusters with close monitoring of fairness percentiles, 3) Full rollout gated by SLO stability. Migration: Added 20260220_reconcile_schema.sql to add pending_credit column to reservation_ledger table and a small migration path included in start-up. Backwards compatibility: New reservation proto field is optional; older agents ignore it. Risk: Medium — policy change under load could affect tail latency; mitigations include conservative defaults, probation fallback, and immediate kill-switch. Merge details: Squash-merged to main after approvals from reviewers; changelog and docs committed. Related work: Follow-ups planned to expose per-tenant trial windows and integrate with predictive headroom scheduler.
review_conversation: Marcos Silva: Please ensure the ledger compare-and-swap handles high concurrency; what about multi-cluster spillover? Lina: Added CAS loop and unit tests simulating 50 concurrent writers; spillover uses existing spill queue and is unchanged. Ariel Thompson: Docs look thin on defaults; can we pick safer conservative defaults? Lina: Set reconciler.defer_window_seconds=300 and apply_rate=0.05 by default and updated docs. Devon Park: If reconciler lag becomes large, we should avoid accepting new prioritized reservations. Lina: Added reconciler_lag_threshold and a fallback to legacy allocation when exceeded.
